data.title: Immutable – Why IMX’s price rally faces risks despite 105% volume surge
data.description:
Immutable [IMX] had a 13% surge in price over the past day at press time,  while activity turned bullish. Investors remain uncertain about whether speculation drives the recent rally or whether bulls have established a strong foothold in the market.

Fundamentally, the sentiment indicator, which gauges investors’ outlook, remains “neutral,” showing that neither bulls nor bears have gained clear conviction.

AMBCrypto analyzed the market conditions to determine what the probable market direction for IMX remains.

Trading volume supports IMX’s bullish price move

The present surge in price hasn’t happened in isolation and is, in fact, backed by bullish volume analysis.

Price and volume share a key relationship that often establishes what actual investors are doing. For context, when price and volume surge simultaneously, it shows that traders are actively backing the price increase.

Currently, CoinMarketCap reports that volume has risen over 105% to $30 million at the time of this analysis. Given the price’s present direction, the clear bias is that investors are fueling the rally.

The majority of the volume has been led by three exchanges, HTX, Binance, and Upbit. Collectively, these venues drive more than 30% of IMX volume in the market.

The presence of HTX and Upbit suggests that Asian investors currently drive a significant share of the trading volume. Both exchanges account for 19.66% of the market volume.

Capital flows show stronger bullish positioning

There’s a clear bullish positioning that, likewise, shows that bulls are actively positioning for further upside more than sellers.

The Open Interest-weighted Funding Rate, an indicator that combines Open Interest, which represents capital in an asset’s perpetual contracts, and the Funding Rate, which reflects the long or short share of that capital. This shows that long traders have a large dominance.

This is based on the OI-weighted Funding Rate staying positive, with a reading of 0.0040% as of writing. A moderately positive Funding Rate suggests that investors have not taken on excessive exposure, which could help support price stability.

Adding to this outlook has been the growing capital inflow into the perpetual market. Often, capital outflow should dominate when there’s a massive price surge, as seen with IMX. In this case, however, investors increased their exposure as Netflow crossed $243,000 in the past 24 hours.

Spot selling and liquidations remain key risks

Spot remains a key threat to any further surge, as this group has continued to sell as the price surged. The spot Netflow reached $364,000 in the past day, as investors capitalized on the gains. More concerningly, the price surge liquidated more long positions than short positions over the past 24 hours.

Putting numbers to it, longs lost roughly $31,000, while shorts lost $21,000. Ideally, in a bullish market condition, shorts often record more losses than longs do, but in this case, it’s the reverse, which should be a note of caution for investors.

Final Summary

  • IMX’s 13% price surge has gained support from rising trading volume and a positive OI-Weighted Funding Rate.
  • Spot selling and higher long liquidations remain key risks that could limit IMX’s continued upside.

data.title: Bitcoin price to $90K? BTC/Gold ratio signals a key liquidity shift
data.description:
As Bitcoin [BTC] consolidates below $90k, the important question is what could eventually push the price higher.

Interestingly enough, a catalyst may already be in place. From a macro perspective, the yields on treasuries are rising, and the probability of a rate hike in October has plummeted to 17% from 75% a few days ago. Nonetheless, the risk appetite remains repressed, and investors are still hedging into safe havens. In other words, liquidity is still cautious.

As analysts at the Kobeissi Letter note:

We just got a weaker than expected September jobs report, a 2-month downward revision of -60,000 jobs, and weaker than expected PCE inflation data. Meanwhile, the 10Y Note Yield can’t even hold a decline for more than one hour. The bond market is not messing around. 

However, looking closer at the situation, it becomes apparent that the relevance of Bitcoin on the macro level is far from being over. As seen on the chart below, the BTC/XAU ratio is pushing higher and looks ready to break above a significant level, which would be the second time since the rotation started in mid-August.

According to AMBCrypto, the liquidity from this rotation could be the catalyst that propels Bitcoin towards $90k. With FOMC related FUD keeping volatility high, a rotation from gold to BTC could provide the liquidity required for a breakout, a view is shared by Jurrien Timmer, Director of Global Macro at Fidelity.

Bitcoin’s macro hedge appeal puts $90k back in focus

When it comes to FOMO, the setup makes it clear why Bitcoin is seeing increased preference over gold.

From a technical lens, the BTC/XAU ratio ended Q3 up 37%+ higher, making it the best quarterly gain since the Q4 2024 election-driven rally. Thus, the BTC price against gold reached a critical level, reaffirming Bitcoin’s status as a macro-hedge. Jurrien Timmer, Fidelity’s Director of Global Macro, highlighted this shift:

I continue to like exposure to both gold and Bitcoin, but especially Bitcoin looks interesting to me at these levels, where we broke out above $80k, targeting $100k.

Interestingly enough, it appears that his BTC preference goes beyond gold. As the post below highlights, Bitcoin only has around a 30% correlation with the S&P 500 and is mostly uncorrelated with treasuries. This makes Bitcoin a useful diversifier if a new four-year cycle is starting to emerge.

In short, since BTC’s correlation with Treasury yields is lower than that of gold, the asset appears to benefit from the rotation and strengthen the BTC/XAU ratio.

Therefore, if the tendency persists, the BTC/XAU breakout could act as an essential liquidity marker. Especially considering that the macro environment remains volatile, Bitcoin’s strength against gold may well enable another $90k leap.

Final Summary

  • BTC is gaining strength against gold as money rotates back into Bitcoin.
  • A BTC/XAU breakout could add liquidity and support a move toward $90k.

data.title: NEAR Intents ends probe after exploiter returns stolen $3.8M
data.description:
NEAR Intents’ hacker returned all the stolen $3.8 million, a day after the exploit was made public. While this was commendable, given the rising number of crypto hacks with limited refunds, the recovery was strikingly interesting. 

The hack was isolated to BNB Chain and targeted an integration bug on the Omni system that runs the NEAR Intents, a cross-chain system that allows users to move funds without the need for bridges. 

This allowed the attacker to siphon off $3.8 million on the 1st of October. The team flagged it using its AI security layer (SHIELD) and shut down NEAR Intents for about an hour to investigate it. 

The attacker was swiftly tracked within 24 hours. Shortly after, NEAR Intents General Manager and Co-Founder of Aurora Labs, Alex Shevchenko, gave him 48 hours to return the funds. 

A few hours after the warning, he confirmed that the attacker had reached out and was willing to negotiate. Later on, he said the funds were fully recovered and added, 

The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents hack were sent back in full. We are stopping the investigation. Please use bug bounties instead of disrupting the services.

Community reactions to NEAR Intents’ $3.8M recovery

The statement “use bug bounties instead” insinuated that the said “attacker” probably defended their action as security research that they were planning to report to the team. 

In fact, Illia Polosukhin, Founder of Near Protocol, also made a similar suggestion and added, 

To echo Alex: for security researchers looking for exploits, we encourage you to use bug bounties. They exist for a reason.

As of writing, the identity of the “attacker” has not been made public. However, this is one of the fastest exploits that have been resolved recently. In fact, it may be the only one where all stolen funds have been recovered within two days.  

In Q3 alone, crypto hack-related loss surged from $86 million at the end of June to $742 million at the end of September. That’s nearly a 10x increase. 

One of the two largest exploits was Bitget’s $388 million and Liquid Network’s $320 million. For Bitget, slightly over $1 million has been frozen out of the $388 million. The Liquid Network incident stands out and rivals NEAR Intent because attackers returned 85% of the funds ($272 million) within 24 hours. 

Notably, over $1.25 billion has been lost since July, with North Korean threat actors flagged as the biggest players. 

That said, NEAR Intents’ resolution could be bullish for the altcoin, according to analyst Michael van de Poppe. The  $NEAR hacker has returned all of the funds. Done deal, resume the bullishness on NEAR.”

However, NEAR extended its losses to 16% and broke below a key trendline support. If the weakness persists, it could hit the next support zone at $4 or $3.5. 

Final Summary

  • NEAR Intents has recovered all the stolen $3.8 million. 
  • The recovery has not boosted NEAR value amid broader market weakness.

data.title: XRP enters critical October week- Can its price finally break $1.50?
data.description:
XRP is set to have a week that will define its October outlook.

In particular, there are four major dates lined up in the first week of the month. First, on the 3rd of October, XRP Seoul will host the banks and Ripple. Then, the Evernorth deal is expected to be completed on the 7th of October, while XRPN is expected to start trading on Nasdaq a day later. Finally, it ends with the XRPL Batch amendment (XLS-56) on the 9th of October.

To put this into context, said amendment already has more than 85% of validators supporting it. The key takeaway? The amendment would empower the ledger to settle up to eight transactions atomically. 

Given the XRP Ledger already processes more than 200 million transactions on average per quarter, this could be a major boost to the network’s capacity, making Q4 an important period for XRPL’s on-chain activity.

Meanwhile, the timing of this upgrade could not be better.

As institutional adoption of the XRPL grows, Evernorth will take its XRP treasury company, XRPN, public on Nasdaq with approximately 473 million XRP on its balance sheet. As such, pre-merger shares have already jumped by 81%, creating another pillar of institutional adoption for XRP’s Q4 setup.

Moreover, this bullish start to October is evident in trader positioning. Binance’s top traders are slowly but surely accumulating XRP long positions, thereby skewing the long/short ratio in favor of the bulls.

And if this inclination continues to build alongside the general flow of catalysts, it may well serve as a powerful catalyst for Ripple’s [XRP] next move.

XRP’s broader setup aligns with a bullish technical structure

Ripple’s October roadmap is coming at a pivotal moment for another reason as well.

From a technical lens, XRP has been consolidating around the $1.50 level for over 4 weeks. If history is any guide, then such a scenario often leads to a sharp move in either direction. But with a catalyst-heavy week ahead and long positioning in place, this range could simply be traders’ positioning ahead of a breakout.

The liquidity picture also points bullish. XRP’s liquidity is distributed over eight exchanges within a ±2% range. More importantly, that liquidity constitutes $18 million in bids versus $14 million in asks. Although the total depth is about $30 million, similar to 2025 levels, the increased bid liquidity gives buyers an edge as XRP nears a key inflection point.

Overall, Ripple’s broader setup seems to be complementing well with the technical pattern and on-chain action for XRP and XRPL. With the upgrades, institutional developments, and long positioning in place, October looks a likely catalyst to propel XRP out of this lengthy consolidation channel.

Final Summary

  • XRP enters October with key XRPL upgrades, institutional developments, and rising long positioning.
  • Strong bid liquidity and a four-week consolidation range could set the stage for a breakout.

data.title: How SKY crypto’s 10x revenue surge could extend its 11% rally
data.description:
Sky [SKY], the native token of decentralized finance protocols, has been on the higher side, with gains crossing 11% in the past 24 hours as of writing.

When analyzed critically, the majority of the gains stemmed from inflows in on-chain activity in the market, especially in terms of revenue.

Revenue generated by SKY moved from a low of $48,500 to roughly $560,800 on the 30th of September, according to data from Artemis. However, the latest data from DeFiLlama confirms that revenue has slid to $436,210 as of writing.

This represents an increase of roughly 10x, confirming that on-chain activity has been on the higher side. A trend of this nature is associated with bullish market conditions, as investors are actively using the protocol more.

More broadly, the protocol is doing well. The yearly Gross Profit had reached its third-highest level, with $137.9 million generated so far, behind 2024 and 2025. The performance at this level is likely to sustain the price in the near term.

SKY’s on-chain activity strengthens

There has been a surge in on-chain activity, with market transactions reaching a high of 1.2 million in the past day.

According to data from Artemis, the number of transactions between since the 25th of September has grown by over 200,000, reaching roughly 1.2 million transactions.

Transaction activity has also aligned with the growth of Daily Active Users on the protocol, which reached 90,800 at the time of writing. The surge in Daily Active Users and transactions aligning together suggests that the activity has a strong hold on the asset’s performance in the market.

Continued activity would mean that SKY’s growth from here is on the higher side, as the tendency is likely to continue in the near term for the asset to perform notably well.

Spot accumulation supports SKY’s performance

Spot market accumulation has been playing a role in feeding the asset’s performance. In the past 24 hours, there has been massive accumulation of roughly $125,000 in SKY, which could influence its performance in the near term.

When there is massive accumulation like this in the past day, it often implies that traders are anticipating that the asset will see a surge in the near term.

This buying trend has been observed across the market over the past fifteen days, with the total accumulation being about $15 million in Netflow. When Netflow is negative, there has been more buying than selling in the market.

If this trend continues along this path, there is a chance that the price in the near term will maintain its performance, adding to price performance.

Final Summary

  • SKY’s revenue surged 799% as on-chain activity and Daily Active Users increased, supporting the token’s recent gains.
  • Negative Netflow points to continued Spot Accumulation, with traders showing stronger buying activity across the market.

data.title: Pump.fun sees $8.3M in long liquidations – Can PUMP defend $0.005?
data.description:
Following a weak jobs report, the broader crypto market was hit hard as investors rushed to reduce exposure. Amid this shift in sentiment, Pump.fun’s [PUMP] downside pressure intensified.

As a result, PUMP faced rejection at $0.0061 and fell to $0.0054 at press time. Over the same timeframe, the altcoin’s trading volume climbed 55% to $605 million, indicating higher sell-side activity.

PUMP long liquidation exceeds $8M

The price drop left longs bleeding. According to Lookonchain, two major traders were liquidated. These traders had opened a long position on 707.6 million PUMP worth $3.61 million.

The liquidation wave extended beyond just two major traders. According to CoinGlass data, PUMP saw over $8.3 million in longs liquidated, compared to $0.7 million in shorts.

Often, prolonged squeezes strengthen downside momentum, leading to even more losses on the charts.

Amid this rising liquidation risk, traders panicked and rushed to close their positions. The altcoin Futures saw $385 million in outflows compared to $374 million in inflows.

As a result, the Futures Netflow declined by 237% to -$10.7 million, a clear sign of aggressive selling.

Historically, intense selling pressure combined with higher liquidation risks has weakened the market structure, leading to further declines.

Can spot demand help absorb the pressure?

Interestingly, despite the price drop and intense pressure from the derivatives market, spot traders have held steady.

On this side, buyers have turned stubborn, and the drop seems to have encouraged them to buy some more. Coinalyze data showed that Spot Buy Volume has outpaced Spot Sell Volume for three consecutive days.

On the 2nd of October, as the market dropped, Buy Volume rose to 25.5 billion compared to 24.6 billion in Sell Volume. 

With buyers holding here, they could likely absorb the pressure and help the market recover from the slip.

What do momentum indicators say?

Structurally, the market still leans bullish. In fact, PUMP has been making higher lows while respecting the rising support.

Despite the pullback, the structure is yet to break down. At the time of writing, the MACD was on an upward trajectory.

The same case applies to the Relative Strength Index (RSI), which was deep in the bullish zone around 62.

Taken together, the MACD and RSI suggest buyers are still in control of the market. If the spot-buying pressure holds, it could absorb downside pressure and help PUMP reclaim $0.006.

However, if sellers in the derivatives market continue at the current pace, PUMP will struggle to hold $0.005 and is likely to drop to $0.0046.

Final summary

  • PUMP faced rejection at $0.0061 and fell 9%  to a low of $0.00509, driven by intense selling pressure. 
  • The price drop triggered a long squeeze, with $8.3 million worth of longs liquidated.

data.title: ‘Exceeded its authority!’ – Banking group sues OCC over crypto trust charter approvals
data.description:
Banks have escalated turf wars with the crypto industry, with OCC trust bank charter approvals becoming the latest battlefield. 

In a new lawsuit against the OCC, the Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) alleged that OCC “exceeded its authority.” 

The OCC has far exceeded its limited statutory authority to charter trust banks that perform certain fiduciary activities. This vast expansion of power creates a gaping hole in financial regulation.

Under the Donald Trump administration, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has granted conditional national trust bank charters to several crypto and fintech firms. These include Ripple, Circle, Paxos, Fidelity Digital Assets, Revolut, Trump-backed World Liberty Financial (WLFI), and more. 

The approval allows the firms to provide asset custody and settlement services nationwide. However, it exempts them from FDIC insurance for consumer deposits. 

For ICBA, this exemption allows crypto firms to enter the banking system under ‘lightly regulated national charters’ rather than more rigorously regulated traditional bank charters. 

For the group, this is unfair competition to community banks, and the uninsured national bank charters could spread financial market instability. 

As such, the ICBA sought the court to vacate the “Final Rule” and Interpretive Letter (IL) 1176, which gave the OCC sweeping powers to charter national trust banks.

Crypto industry slams ICBA lawsuit

The fight between the bank and the crypto industry has been going on for a while. It was evident in the stablecoin yield debate and eventually the stalling of the CLARITY Act. 

Similarly, the banking sector has been publicly opposed to the OCC’s national bank charter approvals. In May, Senator Elizabeth Warren and other Democrats joined the opposition to the OCC’s approvals. 

However, crypto firms didn’t evade regulations but sought them based on the nature of their business, argued The Digital Chamber (TDC), a crypto lobby group. 

OCC’s Jonathan Gould also rejected the banks’ claims, noting that his “job is not about incumbent protection.” So, even though the lawsuit was not surprising, it marks a new escalation in the turf war between the two industries. 

Speaking on the same, Alexander Grieve, VP of Government Affairs at Paradigm, said, 

It’s almost like everything we said about the bank trades just wanting to protect their fiefdoms at the expense of protecting American consumers was true.

It remains to be seen how the lawsuit will pan out. Some policy watchers believe the update could stall the recent SEC push to modernize crypto custody rules. 

But this could also be a tough balancing act for the U.S. government. On one end, it has to deal with an incumbent who wants to protect its turf. On the other hand, it would like to nurture and scale stablecoins to fill in the demand gap for Treasury bills. 

Final Summary

  • Banks want the court to stop and reverse the OCC’s national bank trust charter approvals to crypto firms.
  • The crypto industry opposed the lawsuit as a push for incumbent protection.

data.title: Cardano expands in Japan – So why is ADA’s price down 4%?
data.description:
Is Cardano [ADA] an integral part of the big player story now? The answer is yes.

The Cardano Foundation recently announced Pacific Meta as an Enterprise Integration Partner in Japan, with the goal of helping Japanese companies figure out where Cardano can actually solve business problems and build solutions.

Under the arrangement, the two organizations will share responsibilities. The Foundation handles the infra and technical support. Pacific Meta takes care of the local side: understanding how Japanese enterprises operate, helping with go-to-market, and doing the hands-on systems integration.

AMBCrypto previously reported that Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson expects Midnight [NIGHT] (the privacy-focused network), to become bigger than Zcash [ZEC].

ADA crypto price drops 4% as shorts take over

Has any of this done much for ADA’s price?

Cardano fell to $0.239 in a single hourly candle on the 2nd of October. That’s a reset of most of the day’s gains. Earlier, ADA tested at $0.26 before sellers pushed it back.

At press time, the RSI fell to 30.55, teetering at the edge of being oversold and well below its signal line at 51.59. The Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) also dropped to -0.10; more capital is flowing out of ADA than coming in.

Open Interest fell to about $258.6 million after the drop; some traders closed their positions. Meanwhile, Funding Rate was at -0.0103, so short sellers are now paying to hold their bets against ADA.

A short-term bounce isn’t off the table. But for now, bears have the upper hand.

Final Summary

  • Cardano Foundation partners with Pacific Meta.
  • ADA price drops; funding is negative and shorts took control.

data.title: ‘Privacy working as intended’: Zano details 1-month rollback after $250M exploit
data.description:
The Zano exploit led to over $250 million in fake assets being minted by the attacker. According to a post-mortem report by the project team, the attacker minted 36.89 million ZANO tokens and $18.45 million fUSD, the Freedom Dollar stablecoin. 

During late August and September, the period when the hack happened and the team noticed the exploit, ZANO’s price averaged between $6.50 and $7.50. Assuming an average price of $7.00, the 38.6 million ZANO tokens and $18.4 million fUSD translated to a total of about $250 million in fake assets. 

Earlier in their preliminary investigation, the Freedom Dollar team said that the attacker exchanged “several million dollars” worth of assets for counterfeit fUSD. This has now been verified, as $18.4 million was swapped for fake minted fUSD. 

Before the hack, fUSD, an algorithmic stablecoin on the privacy-focused Zano network, had a market supply of $12 million, or 12 million fUSD tokens. With the hacker minting 18.45 million fUSD, the supply increased by 153%, or 2.5x higher than the base circulation. 

Similarly, about 15.44 million ZANO were in circulation before the breach. After the 36.89 million fake ZANO tokens were minted, the supply was inflated by 240%.

To address the inflation issue, the team opted to roll back the network by a month. 

Zano hack: The mishap, exploit, and recovery

First, the Zano network is privacy-focused, similar to Zcash. 

To scale adoption and plug in more exchanges and platforms, it had to allow external venues to track the amounts being transferred and spent. That’s what the Gateway Address feature in Hard Fork 6 was supposed to solve. The upgrade went live in late August. 

But there was a code error that led to missing verification for Zano transactions. This allowed the attacker to “hide” extra tokens and mix them with the rest of the legit supply. 

The private nature of the transfers made it challenging to trace these fake asset transfers, making the rollback a logical solution, according to the team. While a drawback, the team hailed it as a plus. 

The major limitation was the traceability of the exploited ZANO and fUSD coins. Once created, they were indistinguishable from any other private ZANO output. That is privacy working as intended. No one, including the Zano team, can accurately determine which outputs are affected.

The rollback has erased the $250 million exploit, with the team assuring the network recovery is stable and ongoing. They plan to explore the Gateway Address again later to facilitate broader integration with exchanges. 

But the ZANO token price was still trading close to $5, a key H2 support level, underscoring that investors were still uncertain about the token after the incident. 

Final Summary

  • Zano team confirmed that nearly $250 million worth of fake ZANO and fUSD was minted by the hacker,
  • The network recovery is stable and ongoing, but investor confidence was still low, per the muted ZANO price,

data.title: LayerZero surges 12% – Will $9.07M in selling threaten ZRO’s rally?
data.description:
LayerZero [ZRO] was up 12% at press time, with Binance traders in the market driving the gains, as they remain critical to the asset’s next phase.

Still, this doesn’t eliminate the broader role of traders across the perpetual market who are actively positioning for more upside.

Rising perpetual market volume supports ZRO’s rally

The broader gain in the market has been led by a surge in buying volume across the perpetual market for ZRO specifically.

The volume across the perpetual market for ZRO hit roughly $279 million in the past day, with the Long/Short Ratio staying at 1.56 as of writing. This indicates that the volume in the market is largely coming from long traders.

The context of the buying becomes more insightful when weighed against the Funding Rate of the market. This metric shows whether long or short positions are dominant in a perpetual contract market.

CoinGlass data shows that Binance accounts for the majority of the positions, with the OI-Weighted Funding Rate reaching 0.0066%, suggesting bullish positioning remains dominant.

Binance traders lead the bullish positioning

Binance, among all other cryptocurrency exchanges, controls the most volume across other venues, with data from CoinGlass reporting it at $92.36 million.

The volume dominance shows that the majority of the activity, more than 32% of the total volume, is coming from Binance. Moreover, traders’ actions matter in influencing the price trajectory.

Data shows that Binance traders are fully bullish on the price outlook. Retail traders are accumulating, with buying volume at 1.57. Whales, who control large amounts of capital, are on the same side with a 4.47 Long/Short Ratio, while smart money, which makes profitable bets, is also extremely bullish.

However, liquidation activity in the market warns that going bullish too soon carries a major risk of loss even as the price rallies. Binance traders in the past 24 hours have lost around $74,380, more than short traders’ $47,500 within the same window.

More broadly, losses across the broader market point to the same trend, as a lack of proper positioning has put longs at more than $141,281 in losses over the past 24 hours.

Selling pressure remains a risk to ZRO’s gains

Sellers in the market remain a major concern for what could limit ZRO’s performance in the near term. As it is, spot market flow shows that traders have continued to cash out steadily from the market, with roughly $2.52 million in Netflow, indicating more selling than buying.

This trend has continued over the last ten days, with roughly +$9.07 million in Netflow, confirming that sellers remain active in the market.

Final Summary

  • ZRO’s rally is gaining support from strong perpetual market activity, with Binance traders playing a major role.
  • Rising spot Netflow and liquidation data show that selling pressure remains a risk to ZRO’s gains.
